P.P1_bottleneck_analysis: OS permission check latency (varies by OS). Sensor access bottleneck is real-time data collection (not consent logic).
P.P2_defensibility: Per-sensor consent gives granular control. User can see current permissions. OS and app both must allow (defense in depth).
P.P3_confidence_level: Very high confidence. Standard permission pattern.
P4_failure_modes: OS permission denied → feature blocked (expected, explain to user)
User consent revoked → sensor stops (immediate, verified by audit)
Emergency override scope unclear → wrong data shared (mitigate: clear policy, legal review)
P.P5_backup_plan: If sensor unavailable: degrade gracefully (e.g., use cell location if GPS unavailable).
P.P6_backup_plan_test: Test each sensor individually (enable/disable). Test OS permission denial (simulate by revoking in OS settings). Test emergency override (if implemented).
P.P7_testing_strategy: Unit tests for permission logic. Integration tests for each sensor (GPS, barometer, camera, microphone). End-to-end tests for settings page. Emergency override tests (if applicable).
P.P8_benchmarks: Permission check: <100ms. Sensor access denial: immediate. User setting change: <500ms to take effect.

CH1_change_log.description: Initial CONFolder for sensor consent module

L.L1_legal_considerations: GDPR: location and camera data require explicit consent. CCPA: user control over sensor data. COPPA: parental consent if children. Android: permission scopes (coarse vs fine location). iOS: similar scope model.
L.L3_consent_requirements: Per-sensor explicit consent required. User must understand what each sensor is used for. Ability to revoke without penalty.
L.L4_liability_notes: Over-sharing: sensors enabled without user consent (privacy violation). Mitigation: explicit per-sensor toggles. Under-sharing: features disabled due to missing consent (poor UX). Mitigation: clear explanations, minimum necessary sensors.

F.F3_revenue_impact: Sensor access enables key features (location, emergency detection). Positive impact on retention.

S.S1_cybersecurity: Sensor consent is gate before access (cannot bypass). OS enforces second gate (cannot revoke app permission at app level if OS denies).
S.S2_data_privacy: User controls each sensor independently. Revocation is immediate.
S.S3_encryption_requirements: Sensor data encrypted in transit and at rest (handled by downstream modules).
S.S4_access_control: User controls own sensor permissions. Admin cannot override (unless emergency declared).
S.S5_audit_requirements: Log sensor permission changes. Log sensor access attempts (succeed/fail). Audit trail retention: 1 year.

X.X1_notes: Sensor consent is critical for privacy compliance. Per-sensor toggles give user control. Both user and OS permission required (defense in depth). Emergency override may be needed (EMS accessing location during event).
X2_open_questions: Emergency override: should EMS override user consent? (legal/policy question, requires authorization doc)
Fine vs coarse location: require both permissions? (fine = exact, coarse = approximate)
Barometer: does it require consent? (not PII, but still sensor data)
X.X3_related_research: GDPR location processing requirements. CCPA sensor data control. iOS privacy labels. Android permission model. Emergency legal authorities.
